Reinsurance products are designed to protect an insurer from large, volatile, or accumulated insurance losses.
Reinsurance products have financial features of ceded premium and claim recoveries.
Captive insurance products are designed to finance a corporate group's own risks.
Captive insurance products typically involve risks retained within the group.
Captive insurance products have financial features of risk retention with external protection when needed.
Product classification in insurance can overlap, and the purpose and risk transfer are more important than the label.
